source.recommendation: ITU-R P.833-10 (09/2021), Attenuation in vegetation, Question ITU-R 202/3
source.status: in force, approved 2021-09-27, no revision since
source.nominal_scope: The recommends clause reads 'various models addressing a frequency range from 30 MHz to 100 GHz'. That is a union over disjoint sub models. No single model in the recommendation is validated across it.
source.why_this_file_exists: Recommendation ITU-R P.2040-4 has no vegetation content at all, verified by text search of the in force PDF. Recommendation ITU-R P.1411-13 section 4.5.1 defers entirely to P.833 and adds no number. So P.833 is the only standard that says anything, and this file records what it says and what it does not.

frequency_coverage.gap: Tables 5 to 8 are empty between 12.5 GHz and 37 GHz. At 37 GHz exactly one column exists, London plane in leaf. Every number this study uses in FR3 or FR2 is a nearest neighbour pick across at least 0.4 octaves, and across FR2 across 0.75 octaves onto a single column.
frequency_coverage.figure_2_curve: The specific attenuation graph of section 2.1 is described in the recommendation as 'derived from various measurements over the frequency range 30 MHz to about 30 GHz' with no citation, and the plotted curve stops at about 30 GHz. It carries no table and no in leaf or out of leaf split.
frequency_coverage.maximum_attenuation_Am: Every Am value in the recommendation sits at or below 3.605 GHz. There is no Am anywhere in FR3 or FR2, so the saturating woodland model of equation (1) cannot be closed in this study's bands.

provenance_audit.ret_theory: Johnson, R. A. and Schwering, F., A transport theory of millimeter wave propagation in woods and forests, US Army CECOM-TR-85-1, 1985.
provenance_audit.uk_parameter_set: UK Radiocommunications Agency project AY3880/510005719, final report QINETIQ/KI/COM/CR020196/1.0, Rogers et al., May 2002. Companion measurements at 1.3, 2 and 11.6 GHz reported in Savage et al., Radio Science 38(5) 1088, 2003.
provenance_audit.korean_parameter_set: Entered at P.833-6 (2007) from a Republic of Korea administration contribution. The underlying input documents are members only and were not read.
provenance_audit.millimetre_wave_empirical_anchor: Violette, Espeland and Schwering, pecan orchard measurements at 9.6, 28.8 and 57.6 GHz, 1985, and Schwering, Violette and Espeland, IEEE Trans. Geoscience and Remote Sensing 26, 1988. Three spot frequencies through one orchard in Texas.
provenance_audit.freeze: Tables 5 to 8 have not changed since P.833-5 (2005) for the UK set and P.833-6 (2007) for the Korean set. Figure 2 and its describing sentence are unchanged since P.833-2 (1999).
provenance_audit.silent_rewrite: The sentence 'at frequencies of the order of 1 GHz the specific attenuation through trees in leaf appears to be about 20% greater than for leafless trees' read '10 GHz' in P.833-1 (1994). The anchor frequency moved by a decade in 1999 and the claim has been carried verbatim since.
provenance_audit.orphan_figure: Figure 9 of P.833-10 plots in leaf and out of leaf attenuation at 5, 10 and 40 GHz. The dual slope model that generated it was deleted from the recommendation at P.833-5 in 2005. The figure remains with no generating equation anywhere in the current text. Do not read numbers off it.
provenance_audit.circularity_verdict: Same pattern ROUGHNESS.md found in facade metrology. The theory is one 1985 report, the parameter tables are one 2002 UK project and one 2007 Korean contribution, and the millimetre wave empirical basis is one 1985 Texas orchard at three frequencies. Nothing has been revisited since.

internal_inconsistency.claim: Two models inside the same recommendation disagree by about a factor of three at 11 GHz.
internal_inconsistency.table_8_route: London plane in leaf at 11 GHz has sigma_tau = 0.750 per metre, which is 6.51 dB/m.
internal_inconsistency.figure_2_route: The Figure 2 curve at 11 GHz gives about 2.2 dB/m.
internal_inconsistency.consequence: There is no defensible single optical depth for a canopy in this band, so semantic_twin/foliage.py sweeps it and run_foliage_study.py reports the answer as a function of it rather than as a number.

not_supplied_by_the_recommendation.depolarisation: Section 4 is four sentences about 38 GHz measurements and contains no XPD value, no model and no table. Anything the twin needs about cross polarisation in vegetation has to come from elsewhere and be labelled as such.
not_supplied_by_the_recommendation.phase_function_form: Only alpha and beta are exposed. The functional form of the phase function is never written down, so any renderer has to interpolate it. See semantic_twin/foliage.py sample_phase_function and the delta-M test that bounds the consequence.
not_supplied_by_the_recommendation.leaf_permittivity: The recommendation gives wood permittivity at 40% moisture (Table 10) and no leaf permittivity at any frequency.
not_supplied_by_the_recommendation.canopy_boundary: The recommendation has no interface model, which is correct, because a canopy has no dielectric interface. See canopy_boundary_reflectance.

leaf_volume_fraction.inputs: LAI from ITU-R P.833-10 Table 4, leaf thickness 0.2 mm from Table 9
leaf_volume_fraction.status: derived from the recommendation, not fitted

canopy_boundary_reflectance.model: Maxwell Garnett effective permittivity, eps_eff = 1 + 3 f_v (eps_l - 1)/(eps_l + 2), then normal incidence Fresnel
canopy_boundary_reflectance.status: derived, engineering approximation in the dilute limit
canopy_boundary_reflectance.conclusion: of order 1e-9, roughly 90 dB below the reflectance the P.2040-4 wood substitution gives a tree, so a canopy hull carries no Fresnel interface

figure_2_power_law.status: power law fit to a digitisation of the printed Figure 2, not an ITU printed number, plus or minus 25%
figure_2_power_law.independent_check: Zhang et al., IEEE Wireless Communications Letters, DOI 10.1109/LWC.2019.2899299, section III-B quote about 6 dB/m at 28 GHz from the same figure. This fit gives 5.7.

usage_rule: Never quote a single P.833 derived optical depth for a site in FR3 or FR2. Report the answer against the swept optical depth and state the table envelope, which at 15 GHz spans 0.124 to 0.900 per metre across species, a factor of 7.3.
